statement: `pollDelay` is a field of the clock (`ClockParams.pace`), in blocks: the bound the node honours between a block being final and its own poll having read it, never an observed average. Where the tick is in milliseconds it is at least ceil(tick / slot) + 1 (`pollDelayOf`), and a node that may hold value does not start with less. The daemon checks every poll against it: more final blocks unread than `pollDelay` at the head it saw is a breach, told loud (`poll_late`, with what was unread and the bound), the Entity is told `j_blind` (no forward, no expiry co-signed) exactly as for a provider with no call trace, and the probe waits one full tick, a poll that found nothing unread, before it may end the blindness. The node keeps watching, draining, countering and finalizing. A node that holds no value is never told. The bound enters the hub's gate through the reaction (R-LAG-ONE): a reserve below depth + pollDelay + missed + 1 is refused by `clockParams`.
source: coordinator ruling 10-03 03:32 and 03:50 (reserve bound, hub slack gate); builder; R-DEADLINE-TIMESTAMP; consolidation-plan.md D9

killers.name: R-POLL-DELAY a node whose poll delay is shorter than its own tick implies is not started
R-POLL-DELAY a node that holds no value is never told it was late, whatever it finds unread
R-POLL-DELAY a delivery gives the second of its height's block and the final blocks unread
R-POLL-DELAY a poll later than the bound is told loud and blinds the Entity until one is on time
R-POLL-DELAY a poll with exactly the bound of final blocks unread is on time, one more is late
